overall: The AG found the Melrose Board of Health did not violate the Open Meeting Law: the Feb. 11 notice was sufficiently detailed, an emergency justified the short notice, and two other allegations were declined or outside scope.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Feb. 11 emergency meeting notice, listing vaccine eligibility for people accompanying residents 75+, was insufficiently detailed.
allegations.key_passage: We find that notice posted on February 10 for the Board’s February 11 meeting was sufficiently detailed under the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice was posted less than 48 hours before the Feb. 11 meeting and that no emergency justified the shortened notice.
allegations.key_passage: We are persuaded that the totality of the circumstances following Governor Baker’s announcement expanding vaccine eligibility constituted an “emergency” which allowed the Board to hold a meeting without posting notice 48 hours in advance.

allegations.summary: In his request for further review, the complainant alleged the minutes of the emergency meeting were insufficiently detailed; this was not in the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review this additional allegation as it was not included in the original complaints filed with the public body.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board lacked authority to run the caregiver vaccine eligibility expansion because its clinic was not a state-run site.
allegations.key_passage: As this allegation concerns the Board’s authority, which is outside the scope of the Open Meeting Law, we do not take a position as to the authority of the Board.
